title: Generics & Patterns Recap
concept: A comprehensive recap of generics, interfaces, standard interfaces, and design patterns — connecting all L5 concepts into a unified mental model.
why: Individual concepts are useful. Understanding how they compose — generics + interfaces + patterns — is what separates junior from senior XIOM developers.
theory:
## The L5 Architecture

### Generics: The Foundation

```xiom
fn first[T](items: &Vec[T]) -> T           // Type parameter
fn max[T: Ord](a: T, b: T) -> T           // Constrained generic
pub type Pair[K, V] = { key: K; val: V; }  // Generic type
```

Generics eliminate code duplication. One implementation works for ALL types.

### Interfaces: The Contract

```xiom
pub interface Clone { fn clone(&self) -> Self; }
pub interface Display { fn fmt(&self, f: &mut Formatter) -> Result; }
```

Interfaces define WHAT a type can do. Generics define what types code ACCEPTS.

### Derive: The Automation

```xiom
#[derive(Clone, Eq, Hash, Debug, Display)]
pub type User = { id: Int; name: Str; }
```

Derive macros eliminate boilerplate. Write your type, the compiler writes the interfaces.

### Comptime: The Meta-Layer

```xiom
const TABLE = comptime generate_lookup(256);
comptime assert_eq(BUFFER_SIZE % 64, 0);
```

Comptime moves computation from runtime to compile time — zero overhead.

### Design Patterns: Composition

| Pattern | Uses | Solves |
|---------|------|--------|
| Newtype | Type alias | Type safety |
| Builder | Generics + Default | Complex construction |
| Type State | Phantom generics | Invalid state prevention |
| Strategy | Interfaces + Box | Algorithm selection |
| Visitor | Interfaces + enums | Operation separation |
| Observer | Interfaces + Vec | Event handling |

### The Composition Matrix

```
Generic<T> + Interface = Constrained Generic (T: Ord)
Interface + Box = Runtime Polymorphism (Box[dyn Display])
Generic + Comptime = Zero-Cost Abstraction
Newtype + Invariant = Safe Domain Type
Type State + Invariant = Provably Safe State Machine
```

### When to Use What

```
Need code for multiple types?         → Generics
Need to define behavior contracts?    → Interfaces
Need runtime behavior selection?      → Box[dyn Interface]
Need compile-time guarantees?         → Comptime
Need to prevent type confusion?       → Newtype
Need safe construction?               → Builder
Need safe state transitions?          → Type State
Need swappable algorithms?            → Strategy
Need to add operations to types?      → Visitor
Need event propagation?               → Observer
```
tips: The power of XIOM is composing these concepts — generics + interfaces + patterns
Master the standard interfaces (Clone, Eq, Ord, Hash, Debug, Display, Default) first
Use derive for standard interfaces, implement manually only when needed
Design patterns solve problems — don't force them where simpler code works
common_mistakes: Over-engineering: applying all patterns when 3 lines of code would suffice
Under-engineering: not using generics when you have 3 copies of the same function with different types
Pattern obsession: seeing every problem as a nail for your favorite pattern hammer
